why: One agent, law first then fix, in next/: a fast prefix key is no longer lost in the browser tab. The tab's key listener judged each press against run.getState().prefix, which lags the presses it already sent, because tea's run reads its line after the press must be answered (a fold waits on the Cmds of the one before it). The decision now has one home: handle in next/packages/libfabrika/src/client/WindowMachine.ts reads the presses still waiting in the run's line through the window machine's own update, then routes the new press with Keys.route on the prefix that results. The window model counts the presses it has read (presses), so the listener can tell which of its handed-over presses are still waiting. The listener keeps only that list of waiting presses, never a copy of the model. No key, word or look changed.
